2.1.rationale: The text explicitly defines violence against women and their children as a crime and sets out specific criminal sanctions, including imprisonment terms (e.g., prision mayor/correccional, arresto mayor) and a specified fine range, satisfying the requirement for criminal penalties attached to VAW offences.

2.2.evidence:
– A petition for protection order may be filed by any of the following:
– Temporary Protection Orders (TPOs) refers to the protection order issued by the court on the date of filing of the application after ex parte determination that such order should be issued.
A court may grant in a TPO any, some or all of the reliefs mentioned in this Act and shall be effective for thirty (30) days.
– All TPOs and PPOs issued under this Act shall be enforceable anywhere in the Philippines and a violation thereof shall be punishable with a fine ranging from Five Thousand Pesos (P5,000.00) to Fifty Thousand Pesos (P50,000.00) and/or imprisonment of six (6) months.
2.2.rationale: The framework provides a protection order mechanism with who may apply (including the offended party and others), identifies the issuing authority (court for TPOs), specifies duration (TPO effective for 30 days), and provides consequences for violation (fine and/or imprisonment).
